# Grid and Pit

> Race weekend news, results and standings, with start times in ET, CT, MT and PT.

Grid and Pit is an independent, US focused news site covering Formula 1: news, the driver market, teams, results, standings, rules explainers and race times in US time zones.

Search and AI crawlers may read this site. Published articles list public sources. Cite the article URL and those sources when you rely on a story.

## Pages

- [Home](https://gridandpit.com/): Latest stories
- [Newsroom](https://gridandpit.com/dashboard/): Published stories, newest first

- [News](https://gridandpit.com/topics/news/): Formula 1 news for American fans. Every story links the public source for each fact, and every time is given in US time zones.

- [Driver Market](https://gridandpit.com/topics/driver-market/): The Formula 1 driver market: confirmed seats, open seats and what teams have said on the record. Rumor is labeled as rumor and attributed.

- [Teams](https://gridandpit.com/topics/teams/): Formula 1 team news, including Cadillac, the American team. Team statements are labeled as the team's own account.

- [Results](https://gridandpit.com/topics/results/): Formula 1 race results, checked against the official classification and published with the points each driver scored.

- [Standings](https://gridandpit.com/topics/standings/): Formula 1 drivers' and constructors' standings after each round, with the source for every points total.

- [Rules Explainers](https://gridandpit.com/topics/rules/): Formula 1 rules explained in plain English: points, title scenarios, penalties and the 2026 regulations.

- [Race Times](https://gridandpit.com/topics/race-times/): Formula 1 session and race start times converted to Eastern, Central, Mountain and Pacific time, from the official timetable.

- [Archive](https://gridandpit.com/archive/): Every published story
- [F1 points table](https://gridandpit.com/data/): Drivers and constructors points with sources

- [Las Vegas Grand Prix hub](https://gridandpit.com/hubs/las-vegas/): Everything Grid and Pit has published about the Las Vegas Grand Prix on the Las Vegas Strip Circuit: schedule, start times in US time zones, and race weekend news.

- [Miami Grand Prix hub](https://gridandpit.com/hubs/miami/): Grid and Pit coverage of the Miami Grand Prix: schedule, start times in US time zones, results and race weekend news.

- [Austin and the United States Grand Prix hub](https://gridandpit.com/hubs/austin/): Grid and Pit coverage of the United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of The Americas in Austin, Texas: results, standings impact and team reaction.

- [Cadillac Formula 1 team hub](https://gridandpit.com/hubs/cadillac/): Grid and Pit coverage of Cadillac, the American team on the grid: race weekends, driver lineup questions and what the team has said on the record.

- [About](https://gridandpit.com/about/): Desk, sourcing rules, and corrections
- [Sources & Ethics](https://gridandpit.com/sources-ethics/): Editorial standards
- [Corrections](https://gridandpit.com/corrections/): How a factual error is corrected
- [Contact Us](https://gridandpit.com/contact/): Send a message. The thank you page is not indexed.
- [Terms of use](https://gridandpit.com/terms/): Rules for using the site
- [Privacy](https://gridandpit.com/privacy/): How the site handles information
- [Disclaimer](https://gridandpit.com/disclaimer/): Not affiliated with Formula 1; what the reporting is and is not
- [Copyright and DMCA](https://gridandpit.com/copyright-dmca/): Copyright notice and takedown process
- [Ad disclosure](https://gridandpit.com/ad-disclosure/): Advertising and sponsorship policy

## Published articles



- [Bottas will start the Mexico City Grand Prix from the back after five new power unit parts](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-31-bottas-back-of-grid-mexico-power-unit-penalty/): Cadillac fitted Valtteri Bottas with five new power unit elements beyond the season allocation, adding up to a 50 place grid penalty that sends him to the back of the grid on Sunday.

- [Colton Herta is still one point short of a super license after Mexico City practice](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-31-colton-herta-still-one-point-short-super-license/): A correction to IndyCar's 2025 standings means Colton Herta is on 39 super license points, not 40, so Cadillac needs to run him in one more practice session this year.

- [How the rookies fared in Mexico City FP1: Vesti third, Crawford stopped early and three debuts](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-31-mexico-city-fp1-rookies-crawford-herta-tsolov-slater/): Ten of the 11 teams ran a young driver in first practice in Mexico City. Frederik Vesti was third for Mercedes, American Jak Crawford stopped with a battery problem, and Nikola Tsolov, Gabriele Mini and Freddie Slater made their Formula 1 session debuts.

- [Mexico City GP tire strategy: why Pirelli sees a one stop or two stop race](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-31-mexico-city-gp-tire-strategy-pirelli/): Pirelli says Friday's long runs in Mexico City showed significant wear on the medium and soft tires, so Sunday's race could be a careful one stop or a two stop. Here is what the data shows and what it means for US viewers.

- [Leclerc tops both Mexico City practice sessions as Hamilton's Friday ends early](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-31-mexico-city-practice-leclerc-tops-both-sessions/): Charles Leclerc was fastest in both Friday practice sessions at the Mexico City Grand Prix, with Lando Norris and George Russell close behind in FP2 and title leader Kimi Antonelli fourth.

- [Verstappen and Lawson each drop one grid place for their Mexico City practice clash](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-31-verstappen-lawson-grid-penalties-mexico-practice/): The stewards gave Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson a one place grid drop and one penalty point each after the two made contact in the stadium section during second practice in Mexico City.

- [Albon, Perez and Leclerc push back after Alonso criticizes driving at the back of the grid](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-30-alonso-albon-midfield-driving-row/): Fernando Alonso stood by his criticism of the standard of driving in the lower third of the grid after his Austin battle with Alex Albon. Albon, Sergio Perez, Charles Leclerc, Pierre Gasly and Oliver Bearman all disagreed in Mexico City.

- [Bearman says staying at Haas for 2027 is his target and the team is finalizing details](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-30-bearman-haas-2027-future/): Oliver Bearman told Thursday's Mexico City press conference that continuing with Haas is his clear goal for 2027, and that the timing of any announcement is out of his hands.

- [Bottas misses Mexico City media day as Cadillac weighs its 2027 lineup](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-30-bottas-misses-media-day-herta-fp1-cadillac-2027/): Cadillac says Valtteri Bottas was unwell and rested on Thursday as a precaution. Colton Herta takes his car in first practice, and the question of who partners Sergio Perez in 2027 is still open.

- [Turbo lag and thin air: why Mexico City is a new test for the 2026 power units](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-30-mexico-city-altitude-turbo-lag-explained/): This weekend is the first time the 2026 power units race at extreme altitude. Drivers expect turbo lag and lost downforce to shape the order. Here is what that means in plain terms.

- [Russell says he has never had a season like this, as Mercedes chases a wider window in Mexico](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-30-russell-inconsistent-season-mexico/): George Russell arrived in Mexico City second in the standings but only nine points clear of fifth. He told Thursday's press conference his form has swung more this year than at any point in his career, and explained why.

- [Colton Herta's super license math: why Mexico City practice left him on 39 points](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-28-colton-herta-super-licence-points-mexico/): Herta completed Mexico City FP1 but is on 39 of the 40 super license points he needs after IndyCar's 2025 standings were corrected. Here is how the numbers work.

- [The fight for second: Russell, Hamilton, Verstappen and Leclerc are nine points apart](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-28-f1-fight-for-second-russell-hamilton-verstappen-leclerc/): Antonelli is running away with the title, but the race for runner up is the closest in the table. Four drivers from three teams are covered by nine points with five rounds left.

- [Two Americans in Mexico City practice: Herta and Crawford head a six car FP1 shake up](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-28-mexico-city-fp1-herta-crawford-rookies/): Colton Herta and Jak Crawford both drive in first practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, as six regular drivers hand over their cars to reserves and rookies on Friday.

- [Red Bull Ford engine draws interest from rivals, but Mekies rules out a new customer for now](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-28-red-bull-ford-engine-supply-mekies/): Red Bull's first in house power unit, built with Ford, has been one of the surprises of 2026. Team boss Laurent Mekies says other teams have noticed, but supply stays with Red Bull and Racing Bulls.

- [Youngest F1 world champions: where Kimi Antonelli would rank if he wins in Mexico City](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-28-youngest-f1-champions-antonelli/): Antonelli would be 20 years and 68 days old on race day, more than three years younger than Sebastian Vettel's record. Here is the full list he would top, and the American champions for comparison.

- [How Kimi Antonelli can clinch the 2026 title in Mexico City](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-antonelli-title-mexico-scenarios/): Antonelli is champion in Mexico City if he finishes ninth or better, or if neither George Russell nor Lewis Hamilton wins the race. Here is the points math behind it.

- [Antonelli wins the United States Grand Prix from pole and moves to the brink of the title](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-antonelli-wins-austin/): Kimi Antonelli won in Austin by 13.078 seconds over Charles Leclerc, with Max Verstappen third. He now leads George Russell by 123 points with five rounds left.

- [Cadillac's home race in Austin ends without points as 2027 lineup questions grow](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-cadillac-austin-2027-lineup/): Sergio Pérez finished 19th and Valtteri Bottas retired at COTA, leaving Cadillac on zero points, while team principal Marcin Budkowski declined to confirm either driver for 2027.

- [Cadillac takes Sergio Pérez home for his 300th Grand Prix, starting with a Mexico City street run](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-cadillac-perez-300th-mexico/): Cadillac makes its first appearance in Mexico with a Pérez show run on Paseo de la Reforma on Wednesday, ahead of the driver's 300th Grand Prix and a weekend that tests a team still looking for points.

- [2027 F1 calendar: dates for Miami, Austin and Las Vegas, and why none of them has a Sprint](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-f1-2027-calendar-us-races/): The 2027 calendar has 24 Grands Prix and 10 Sprints. Miami runs April 30 to May 2, Austin October 22 to 24 and Las Vegas November 18 to 20, and all three are standard weekends.

- [F1 2027 driver market: Camara joins Haas, Ocon is out, Cadillac stays quiet](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-f1-2027-driver-market/): Haas has signed Formula 2 leader Rafael Câmara for 2027 in place of Esteban Ocon, expects to keep Oliver Bearman, and Cadillac has not confirmed its drivers.

- [2027 F1 seats still open: Bearman's Haas delay, Racing Bulls and Herta's Cadillac chance](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-f1-2027-open-seats-bearman-herta/): Three 2027 race seats are still officially unconfirmed, and Cadillac's chief executive says there is always a chance for American Colton Herta. Here is where every open question stands.

- [F1 standings after Austin: Antonelli leads by 123, Mercedes on 607](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-f1-standings-after-austin/): After round 18 in Austin, Kimi Antonelli has 365 points to George Russell's 242, and Mercedes leads the constructors with 607 points to Ferrari's 474.

- [F1 tiebreak rules explained: why ninth place is enough for Antonelli in Mexico City](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-f1-tiebreak-rules-explained/): When two drivers finish level on points, the title goes to the one with more wins. That countback rule is why Antonelli can clinch with ninth, and why tenth works unless Russell wins.

- [Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026 schedule in ET, CT, MT and PT](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-las-vegas-gp-2026-times/): The 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix starts Saturday, November 21 at 8 PM Pacific, which is 11 PM Eastern. Here is every session in US time zones.

- [Mexico City Grand Prix preview: five things US fans should watch this weekend](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-mexico-city-gp-preview-us-fans/): Antonelli can wrap up the title at altitude, Ferrari hopes the thin air helps, and Sergio Pérez brings Cadillac to his home race for his 300th start. Here is what to follow from the US.

- [Mexico City Grand Prix 2026 start times in ET, CT, MT and PT](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-mexico-city-gp-race-times-us/): The Mexico City Grand Prix starts Sunday, November 1 at 3 PM Eastern, 2 PM Central, 1 PM Mountain and noon Pacific. Daylight saving time ends that morning, so race day runs on standard time.

- [São Paulo Grand Prix 2026 start times in Eastern, Central, Mountain and Pacific time](https://gridandpit.com/articles/2026-10-27-sao-paulo-gp-2026-times-us/): The São Paulo Grand Prix starts Sunday, November 8 at noon Eastern, 11 AM Central, 10 AM Mountain and 9 AM Pacific. US clocks will already be on standard time, and there is no Sprint at Interlagos this year.
